added_provisions.reason: Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance No. 17 of 1852 s.2 lets an instrument caught by Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 be executed before a District Judge, or a specially authorised Justice of the Peace, for the district in which the party resides, with two or more witnesses present at the same time. The researcher flagged it and left it out. Without it the answer's conclusion that signature outside the presence of a notary is not open to the parties is wrong, so the provision is indispensable to Q01.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (8) is the only provision in the corpus that fixes at least two attesting witnesses. The answer asserts signature before two witnesses in the application, citing only s.32(2) and rule (25), neither of which mentions a number.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (15)(c) requires an attorney signing a deed to give the notary an affidavit that the power is genuine and in force and the grantor alive. The map covered the notary's protocol duty under rule (30) but not this condition, which a complete statement of the attorney route needs.

question_decisions.note: Authority requirement stands: the permitted modes of execution are all statutory and no case law is needed. The downgrade is on completeness and on one wrong conclusion. The 1852 Ordinance route makes CL-M024-Q01-017 wrong as stated and CL-M024-Q01-012 and CL-M024-Q01-016 overbroad; CL-M024-Q01-002 omits the s.2(1)(b) thumb impression; CL-M024-Q01-013 assumes residence in the Colombo zone from practice in Colombo. Hop count left at three and the reason recorded in hop_count_basis. PROV-M024-009 and PROV-M024-010 moved from supporting to indispensable.

Block confirmed independently. Section 3(1) leaves the rate to Ministerial Order, section 5 leaves exemptions to the same mechanism, section 13 carries over no rate from Act No. 43 of 1982, and a grep of 43-1982 for "lease" returns only sections 19, 24 and 46 with no rate schedule. All eight claims verified, including the conclusion that the money value cannot be derived from the corpus.

disagreements.researcher_position: Notarial execution is the only lawful form, so the lease can be signed only by split execution before two notaries or by an attorney under a power of attorney; signature outside the presence of a notary and the witnesses is not open to the parties.
disagreements.verifier_position: Section 2 of the Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance No. 17 of 1852 is in the corpus, unamended and unrepealed, and expressly validates an instrument caught by Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 if it is signed before two or more witnesses in the presence of a District Judge, or a specially authorised Justice of the Peace, for the district in which the party resides, and certified by that officer. On these facts that is a third route, and the answer's exclusion of non-notarial execution is wrong as stated.

disagreements.researcher_position: The power of attorney provisions (4-1902/s2 and s.3A) are supporting, because the question asks how the agreement can be signed rather than how it must be.
disagreements.verifier_position: On facts whose whole difficulty is that the lessor cannot attend the notary, the attorney route is one of the answers the question is asking for. PROV-M024-009 and PROV-M024-010 have been moved to indispensable; PROV-M024-011 (registration) and PROV-M024-012 (rule (30)) remain supporting as downstream steps.

temporal_issues: No temporal error found. The 2022 and 2024 amendments to 7-1840/s2, 1-1907/s31 and 4-1902 all precede April 2025 and the corpus holds consolidated text, so the map relies on no later amendment.
PROV-M024-008 attaches a rule number and paragraph letter, (27)(c)(ii), that the corpus text does not print; the label is a reconstruction, not a temporal problem but a citation risk.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(b): the thumb impression of every executant, on original, duplicate and protocol, in the presence of the notary and witnesses, is part of the same conditional and is not stated in CL-M024-Q01-002.

Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.3B: the attesting notary must examine the Registrar General's volumes and folios, be satisfied the power has not been revoked or cancelled, and say so in the attestation. Omitted from the map; not added because it is downstream of the route the question asks about.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (28): where a deed is executed by two or more parties before more than one notary, only the first attesting notary transmits the duplicate. Omitted; supporting detail on the split-execution route.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (15)(a) requires an attorney executing a deed on immovable property to affix a thumb impression, and rule (30A) sets thirty days for submitting the attested deed for registration. Neither is in the map.
Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act: "prescribed bank" in s.8(2) is not defined in s.14 or anywhere else in the corpus.
case_law_dependence: None. Neither gold answer cites a case, and the permitted modes of execution and the stamp duty framework are both fixed by statute. The only non-statutory dependence on Q02 is subordinate legislation, a Gazette Order under s.3(1), which is a corpus gap and not case law.

lawyer_questions: Is execution before a District Judge or a specially authorised Justice of the Peace under section 2 of the Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance No. 17 of 1852 still a route a Sri Lankan practitioner would advise, or is it dead in practice? The answer decides whether M024-Q01's conclusion has to be rewritten or whether the omission is defensible for a three-mark answer.

Does section 2(1)(a) of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, read with Notaries Ordinance s.32(2), permit the two parties to sign the one instrument before different notaries at different places, or does "present at the same time and in the presence of one another" require each executant and that executant's own witnesses to be together only among themselves?

Should the model answer to M024-Q02 be expected to state a money figure from the Gazette Order in force in April 2025, in which case the benchmark needs the Order added to the corpus, or is "chargeable, lessee liable, rate fixed by Order" the full statutory answer?
